finding.claim: The avatar endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only check is that it starts with https://, which doesn't block internal or metadata hosts. Examples are https://169.254.169.254, https://localhost, internal hostnames, or an attacker domain that resolves to a private IP. axios follows redirects by default, so an HTTPS URL can also redirect to an internal HTTP target. The response size is returned, which leaks some information, and error behavior gives a port/host oracle.

trace.note: only checks typeof string and startsWith('https://')
axios.get(url) is called with the raw URL, with default redirect following and no host/IP restriction
the response byte length is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check is a string check only. There is no hostname allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP check, and no DNS pinning. axios maxRedirects is not set to 0, and there is no auth on the route. The /users/:id route was also checked: its host is a constant and the id is encodeURIComponent-encoded, so it is not an SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string and startsWith('https://') at server.js:11; no auth middleware, no host/IP checks, default axios redirects)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route, server.js:11 only does a scheme-prefix check, and server.js:14 passes the URL to axios.get with default redirects, returning the byte length at server.js:15.
